Lecture outlines

A proposed path from exact planning to learning from experience and modern applications. Each outline includes learning objectives and preparation.

Proposed teaching plan. Lecture topics and their sequence are a draft for this semester. Dates follow the departmental timetable and public university calendar; holiday teaching adjustments remain subject to the separate university notice.
  • 01

    Sequential decisions and dynamic programming

    States, actions, policies and long-term objectives. Solve a small route-planning problem by backward induction.

    Outline & readingsStudy guide
    Lecture
  • 02

    Finite-horizon DP and shortest paths

    The principle of optimality, deterministic finite-state models, and backward computation on a layered graph.

    Outline & readings
    Lecture
  • 03

    Stochastic dynamic programming

    Random transitions, feedback policies, and expected total cost in inventory and stopping problems.

    Outline & readings
    Lecture
  • 04

    Infinite-horizon problems

    Discounting, stationary policies, Bellman equations, and the intuition behind contraction.

    Outline & readings
    Lecture
  • 05

    Value iteration and policy iteration

    Policy evaluation, policy improvement, and algorithms for solving a known finite MDP.

    Outline & readings
    Lecture
  • 06

    Approximate DP and information states

    The limits of exact computation, rollout and approximate values, with an introduction to partial observations.

    Outline & readings
    Lecture
  • 07

    Lab 1: resource-constrained path planning

    Use an expanded state to plan a route under a resource budget and examine computational tradeoffs.

    Outline & readings
    Lab
  • 08

    Learning from interaction and bandits

    The RL problem, sampled experience, and exploration versus exploitation in multi-armed bandits.

    Outline & readings
    Lecture
  • 09

    Monte Carlo methods

    Learning values from complete episodes, Monte Carlo control, and on-policy versus off-policy data.

    Outline & readings
    Lecture
  • 10

    Temporal-difference learning and control

    Bootstrapping, TD prediction, SARSA and Q-learning, using a common tabular environment.

    Outline & readings
    Lecture
  • 11

    Multi-step learning and planning with experience

    The relationship between Monte Carlo and TD, n-step returns, and combining planning with learned experience.

    Outline & readings
    Lecture
  • 12

    Function approximation and deep Q-learning

    Generalization beyond value tables, linear approximation, and key design choices in deep Q-learning.

    Outline & readings
    Lecture
  • 13

    Policy gradients and actor-critic methods

    Direct policy optimization, REINFORCE, variance reduction and actor-critic methods.

    Outline & readings
    Lecture
  • 14

    Reinforcement learning for language models

    Text generation as a decision process, preference feedback, verifiable rewards, and an introduction to RLHF and reasoning.

    Outline & readings
    Lecture
  • 15

    Lab 2: learning for sequential decisions

    Evaluate learned policies on a small dynamic decision problem; an LLM-related extension is an optional project direction.

    Outline & readings
    Lab
  • 16

    Synthesis and project discussion

    Connect modeling, planning, learning and approximation; discuss experiments and revisit the semester's core ideas.

    Outline & readings
    Review
